correctness.rationale: For \(K_{a,b,c}\), global domination is proved equivalent to meeting all three parts. Coalition compatibility therefore depends only on support union. The upper bounds are derived from the partition defect \(d=N-|\Pi|\): the unique smallest-part vertex forces at most \(a+1\) blocks when \(c=1\); defect at most one is impossible when \(c=2\); and defect at most two is impossible when \(c\ge3\) because either a size-at-least-three part has no singleton (already forcing defect at least three) or singleton blocks in all three parts force three distinct complementary mixed blocks. Explicit constructions attain all bounds. A direct set-partition enumeration independently corroborates all 31 sorted profiles of orders \(3\) through \(10\). The finite check is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact tripartite case is the first complete-multipartite level beyond the source's exact bipartite family. The theorem turns the source's lower bound into a full classification, reveals sharp transitions at \(c=1\) and \(c=2\), and supplies a reusable support-defect method. It is not a routine numerical substitution: two regimes require new upper bounds not implied by the published lower bound.
